output:
To: ashbourne-terrace-chimney
Replying to: p05
Cc: none
Subject: none

Mick, Priya, I walked past at 7 this morning and had a look from the pavement opposite. I'm a chartered structural engineer, but this is me speaking as a neighbour who looked from across the road, nothing more. It's not an inspection and not professional advice. Please do read it though.

Mick, I know you mean well, but please don't go into 43 at 9. About 1.2m of the stack on 41 is still standing. It's leaning towards 43 and the mortar at its base is badly washed out. More gusts around 50mph are forecast this afternoon. If it goes, it comes down through the same hole in 43's roof, and standing under that hole putting props in is about the worst place anyone could be. The floors may be loaded with debris, and right now nobody knows how the weight is getting down through the building. Props in the wrong place can make it worse. The same goes for looking at the loft from inside: please don't. Leave it to the council's dangerous structures team.

JoJo, your cousin isn't wrong that Victorian terraces are generally robust. But this one is damaged, and that's a different thing. There's a stepped crack 5-10mm wide running from the top of the bay up to the first floor window, and the top of the bay looks like it has dropped slightly.

On the pavement, the council tape only goes across 43's front garden, not the footway. There are loose slates along the gutter line of 43 and 45, directly above where people walk. Please use the other side of the road until the council has been, especially on the school run to St Dunstan's. The council already know about the house, but nobody has closed the footway. If you ring them, ask about that specifically. Out of hours it's the main council number.

Priya, about Mrs Doherty: it isn't my decision to make. From the street the front of 45 looked undamaged, and the stack sits on the 41/43 wall, not hers. But I couldn't see the party wall between 43 and 45 from the front. I wouldn't sleep in the front room tonight. If she has family she could stay with until 45 has been checked, I think that would be better.
